document.title: SHSAT Mathematics / NYS Algebra I Foundations
document.source: Curated from NYS Next Generation Mathematics Learning Standards and the NYC SHSAT mathematics specification

standards.title: Operations with signed numbers and order of operations
standards.description: Fluently add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational numbers including negatives; apply order of operations with nested grouping symbols and exponents.

standards.title: Fractions, decimals, and percents
standards.description: Convert flexibly among fractions, decimals, and percents; compute percent increase, decrease, and percent-of-a-percent; solve reverse percent problems (finding the original amount).

standards.title: Ratios, rates, and proportional reasoning
standards.description: Set up and solve problems using ratios, unit rates, and proportions, including scale, mixture, and part-to-part versus part-to-whole distinctions.

standards.title: Rate-time-distance and work problems
standards.description: Solve constant-rate problems relating distance, rate, and time, including combined and opposing rates and shared-work scenarios.

standards.title: Interpret and manipulate algebraic expressions
standards.description: Interpret parts of an expression (terms, factors, coefficients); combine like terms; apply the distributive property including distributing a negative across parentheses.

standards.title: Factoring and expanding quadratic expressions
standards.description: Expand binomial products; factor quadratics with leading coefficient 1 and simple cases with leading coefficient greater than 1; recognize difference of squares and perfect-square trinomials.

standards.title: Create equations from verbal descriptions
standards.description: Translate verbal statements and word problems into one-variable equations and inequalities, defining variables precisely and checking solutions against the original story.

standards.title: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable
standards.description: Solve multi-step linear equations and inequalities, including variables on both sides, fractional coefficients, and the sign flip when multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative.

standards.title: Solve quadratic equations
standards.description: Solve quadratics by factoring, square roots, and the quadratic formula; recognize that a product equal to zero requires a factor equal to zero; account for both square roots.

standards.title: Solve systems of two linear equations
standards.description: Solve two-variable linear systems by substitution and elimination; interpret no-solution and infinitely-many-solution cases; translate word problems into systems.

standards.title: Interpret linear functions, slope, and intercepts
standards.description: Compute and interpret slope as a rate of change; find and interpret intercepts; write linear equations from two points, a point and a slope, or a table or graph.

standards.title: Angles, triangles, and polygon relationships
standards.description: Apply angle relationships (vertical, supplementary, parallel lines with transversals), triangle angle sum, exterior angles, and interior angle sums of polygons.

standards.title: Perimeter, area, and volume
standards.description: Compute perimeter and area of triangles, quadrilaterals, circles, and composite figures, and volume and surface area of prisms and cylinders; keep units and squared/cubed distinctions straight.

standards.title: Coordinate geometry and the Pythagorean theorem
standards.description: Use the Pythagorean theorem, distance and midpoint on the coordinate plane, and slopes of parallel and perpendicular lines.

standards.title: Averages, weighted averages, and central tendency
standards.description: Compute and reason about mean, median, mode, and range, including weighted averages, changing an average by adding or removing a value, and average speed as total distance over total time.

standards.title: Counting and probability
standards.description: Solve counting problems using the multiplication principle and simple permutations and combinations; compute probabilities of single and compound independent events.

misconceptions.title: Fails to distribute a negative
misconceptions.description: Distributes only to the first term inside parentheses when subtracting a group, e.g. 5 - (x + 3) becomes 5 - x + 3.

misconceptions.title: Sign errors multiplying/dividing negatives
misconceptions.description: Believes a negative times a negative is negative, or loses track of signs across several multiplications.

misconceptions.title: Left-to-right order of operations
misconceptions.description: Evaluates strictly left to right, e.g. 3 + 4 × 2 = 14, ignoring multiplication precedence.

misconceptions.title: Exponent means multiply by the exponent
misconceptions.description: Computes x^2 as 2x, or 3^4 as 12.

misconceptions.title: Adds fractions across numerators and denominators
misconceptions.description: Computes 1/2 + 1/3 as 2/5 by adding tops and bottoms separately.

misconceptions.title: Inverts the wrong fraction when dividing
misconceptions.description: For a ÷ b/c, flips a instead of b/c, or multiplies without flipping at all.

misconceptions.title: Uses the wrong base for percent change
misconceptions.description: Computes percent change against the new value instead of the original, or applies a discount-then-tax to the wrong base.

misconceptions.title: Treats successive percents as additive
misconceptions.description: Believes a 20% increase followed by a 20% decrease returns to the original, or that 10% + 10% increases equal one 20% increase.

misconceptions.title: Confuses part-to-part with part-to-whole
misconceptions.description: Given a ratio of boys to girls 2:3, treats 2/3 as the fraction of the class that is boys instead of 2/5.

misconceptions.title: Uses additive instead of multiplicative scaling
misconceptions.description: Scales a recipe or similar figure by adding the same amount to each quantity rather than multiplying by the ratio.

misconceptions.title: Averages the two speeds
misconceptions.description: For a round trip at different speeds, averages the speeds arithmetically instead of using total distance over total time.

misconceptions.title: Combines unlike terms
misconceptions.description: Adds terms with different variables or powers, e.g. 3x + 2x² = 5x³ or 2x + 3 = 5x.

misconceptions.title: Drops the middle term when squaring a binomial
misconceptions.description: Expands (x + a)² as x² + a², losing the 2ax middle term.

misconceptions.title: Wrong signs when factoring
misconceptions.description: Chooses factor-pair signs that give the right product but wrong sum, e.g. factoring x² - x - 6 as (x - 2)(x + 3).

misconceptions.title: Operates on one side of an equation
misconceptions.description: Adds or divides on one side only, breaking equality while 'moving' terms.

misconceptions.title: Moves a term without changing its sign
misconceptions.description: Transposes terms across the equals sign keeping the same sign, e.g. x + 5 = 12 becomes x = 12 + 5.

misconceptions.title: Doesn't flip the inequality with negatives
misconceptions.description: Divides both sides of an inequality by a negative number without reversing the inequality symbol.

misconceptions.title: Solves a quadratic like a linear equation
misconceptions.description: Given x² = 25 answers only x = 5, missing the negative root; or moves x² terms as if linear.

misconceptions.title: Misapplies the zero-product property
misconceptions.description: Sets factors equal to the constant instead of zero, e.g. from (x-2)(x-3) = 6 concludes x = 8 or x = 9... or x-2 = 6.

misconceptions.title: Substitutes into the same equation
misconceptions.description: Solves one equation for a variable and substitutes back into that same equation, producing 0 = 0 and confusion.

misconceptions.title: Inverts slope as run over rise
misconceptions.description: Computes slope as change in x over change in y, or mixes coordinate order between the two points.

misconceptions.title: Variable as label instead of quantity
misconceptions.description: Writes equations like 3s = d for 'three students per desk' reversing the relationship (the classic students-and-professors error).

misconceptions.title: Confuses supplementary and complementary
misconceptions.description: Uses 90° where 180° is required (or vice versa) for angle pair relationships.

misconceptions.title: Conflates area and perimeter
misconceptions.description: Adds side lengths when area is asked, multiplies when perimeter is asked, or forgets squared units.

misconceptions.title: Misplaces the hypotenuse in the Pythagorean theorem
misconceptions.description: Writes a² + c² = b² with the hypotenuse as a leg, or adds legs directly without squaring.

misconceptions.title: Averages averages without weighting
misconceptions.description: Combines group averages by taking their simple mean, ignoring different group sizes.

misconceptions.title: Adds probabilities of independent events
misconceptions.description: Computes the probability of two independent events both happening by adding instead of multiplying.

misconceptions.title: Overcounts ordered arrangements
misconceptions.description: Uses permutations where order doesn't matter, double-counting selections (or the reverse).
